item.title: Re: The Song of Your Life (Seeking Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Well since I'm unable to edit my page currently, I'm just going to throw in an idea for the Central Narrative that hit me like a truck.

Central Narrative: As above with potentially exploring other SCP's stories and personalities through the radio's music. Eventually (I don't really know how planned interviews and addendum later down the SCP's life-line works) I'm planning for a researcher to try and ask the SCP questions, the SCP answers in a semi-convoluted way.

Standard questions apply and then… the researcher will go to ask 'do you have a song of yourself?'

The radio will reply 'no' but will than go onto say, 'but I'm sure I did have one, but I don't anymore.'

And like… that could go down so many routes, who took it? Where is it now? How do we get it? What happens when the SCP gets its 'song' back?

Does the Foundation fulfill its request? The SCP probably has some hints in its memory of where the song once was and that can go into tales or more interviews and mission ops and lot of other things.

So that's a narrative I've come up with.

item.title: The Dover Demon
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy/History

Elevator Pitch: SCP-X is the creature known as The Dover Demon. SCP-X is a small humanoid with bright white eyes lacking pupils, with a large skull and and no mouth, however it is able to speak, with its face moving as if it is speaking. It also has 4 long fingers. SCP-X is also able to become invisible, to hide itself from others. SCP-X is very friendly (and rather humorous) and likes interacting with trusted individuals. It typically walks on its two hind legs, but if it is running, runs on four legs.

+ Central Narrative
- Hide

The main focus of the article will be centered around an interview conducted with SCP-X shortly after its recovery. SCP-X is asked about where its from. This leads to a brief explanation that he was born in a cave, and that once he was around 19 he left his family. He then set off to explore the world and its numerous wonders. (Which he states was around 1600 he would typically spend long amounts of time wandering the world and exploring new places.) He soon traveled to England, undetected because of his ability to become invisible. He claimed to have met Queen Elizabeth I, before leaving England on the mayflower, and arriving in America.

He claims to have secretly settled with the pilgrims, and lived in Massachusetts from 1620-1780, where he claims to have witnessed some of the earliest thanksgivings, several witch trials, the Boston massacre, witnessed several battles of the Revolutionary War, and met Benjamin Franklin. He then claims to have traveled west, and seen several landmarks, such as The Grand Canyon, the Rio Grande, the Mississippi river, and Lake Michigan.

SCP-X claims to have traveled back to New England in the early 1800's, where he indirectly causes the destruction of a textile mill, meets James Monroe, and in the late 1890's helps create the first plane, un-pubically. SCP-X claims to have watched news reports on the sinking of the Lusitania, the bombing of pearl harbor, the bombing of Hiroshima, and the death of Adolf Hitler.

He also briefly covers how he was travelling through dover in the 1970's, lining up with the "Dover Demon sightings" made by William Bartlett, John Baxter, and Abby Brabham. SCP-X's life was for the most part uneventful from then until its capture by the foundation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think the attention grabber that the foundation literally has a little guy telling tales about battles of the Revolutionary war, (and possibly the unique idea around this concept?)

Additional Notes: I've always had some interest in the Dover Demon, and thought of this idea that might fit him. Give me your critiques and tell me what you think!

item.title: Re: "Long" Beach California (Seeking Feedback)
item.content:encoded:
Hey there BUCKSHOT74, I’ll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am not an official reviewer, so take what I say with a grain of salt. With that said, let’s begin the crit!

+ Open Section-by-Section
Woooooosh

Elevator Pitch

So it’s a beach 60 miles1 south of Long Beach where the water seems 80-90 yards2 away, yet never gets closer. To be honest, I’m not too keen on this idea (by itself). It isn’t very interesting in my opinion (all it is is a beach where the water doesn’t get closer), and seems to simply be the opposite of SCP-2684. However, if a good narrative is applied to it, it still could work.

Central Narrative

The narrative here consists of the Foundation sending out people to find out what’s up with the beach, and that’s about it. Some people die, they find some writing (which you proceed to not tell us about), and there’s a vague notion of a tall, mysterious entity that kills everyone who saw it. Personally, I don’t really like this. There isn’t any deeper narrative or explanation as to why the beach appeared, it just boils down to people being killed, which I find uninteresting.

Hook/Attention Grabber

The dry-drowning premise is unique[…]

Unfortunately, it isn’t. SCP-1812 is an excellent example of a dry-drowning premise that is in-theme, where we see the dry-drowning is due to the perceived higher gravitational pull on Earth’s water. In your idea, we don’t have an explanation as to why the first D-Class suddenly drowned, they just did. Oddly, they drowned at 8kms out rather than much sooner (which would make sense with the water depths of the average beach), and I’d like an explanation.

Also, as I explained earlier, the narrative is kind of boring, so the audio logs wouldn’t keep the reader entertained.

+ Open General Thoughts
I don’t know about this

The idea is (in my opinion) relatively boring, the narrative isn’t interesting and doesn’t give any explanation for the beach or entity, and the unique concept in your hook isn’t unique. Unless you overhaul the narrative to this, I don’t think your concept would survive on the mainsite.

Anyway, that’s it for my crit today. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!

Footnotes
1. Metric, not imperial, is the system used on the Site.
2. Metric.

item.title: Re: I Am Requesting A Greenlight On A Concept
item.content:encoded:
Hello Dr Camero! lets take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: A katana, longbow, and samurai armor, with anomalous properties, crafted using an unknown element.

What are the anomalous properties? what does the skip do? does it have a purpose? what is this 'unknown element'?-what part does this have in the narrative? what about this will make me as the reader care?

-Currently the skip doesn't really show anything outwardly interesting or unique, as it doesn't have much going for it other than the effects (which themselves are quite vague). As a result, the skip comes across as a bit cliched and dime a dozen, as there are already a fair few amount of sword and weaponry related articles on the main-site, and this concept (in its current state) doesn't seem to bring anything new to the table. Which in turn, makes it hard for me get invested in the idea, or confident that it would work in its current state.

The narrative:

Central Narrative: A katana that is forged from an unknown smith, a longbow with arrows that will seek the wielders target, and armor that is practically unbreakable.

This is closer to additional info than a story, there isn't any sort of setup, middle act, payoff or conflict shown here. How will the current idea fit into a narrative?- what would the article look like? What direction will the story take? are there any characters? how does the Foundation get involved? whats the main conflict? whats everything building up to? what will make me as the reader invested in this?

I would highly recommend starting development on a narrative, as they can help with audience engagement and can further explain the skip. Modern audiences tend to favour skips with a narrative, which has lead to them more or less becoming the standard. The narrative doesn't need to be a long winded saga, short stories can work very well if done right.

Hook:

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The sword can drain exact amounts of blood, and heal wounds perfectly once the blood is lost. The longbow can shoot arrows at unnatural speeds and the arrows can always hit their mark. The armor is from a time period that didn't exist when it was made, and can't be destroyed.

This isn't really much of a hook, it's more or less a bunch or specific effects which alone don't keep my interest as there isn't much behind them. What part does this play in the story? whats their purpose?

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

-RED

item.title: The Song of Your Life (Seeking Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Musical

Page Layout (Optional): Basic layout

Elevator Pitch:
-SCP is a sentient vintage ham radio that produces various forms of music to living things that enter its radius.
-The music in-question is based off the person's history, personality, how other people view them and in the case of other SCPs or other anomalous entities, their abilities. It can also play music to what would otherwise fit the scenario in-question (if its a containment breach its going to sound out chase music mixed in with the leitmotifs of the other SCPs that are part of the breach, etc, etc.)
-The SCP can teleport to a place that is having a suitably dramatic moment and play said music or otherwise to a person that it has played music to before and is 'bored.'

Central Narrative: Don't have a narrative per say, but it could possibly shed light on other SCP's stories and personalities through song.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I've looked at a lot of other SCPs and while there are a couple that play songs, I haven't really seen any from my digging about that basically plays a person or SCP's own personal theme song or opera in some-cases and the fact that there is a chance for a lot of interactions with other SCPs throughout the base or the researchers in-general makes me feel like there's a lot of potential for The Song of Your Life.

Additional Notes: No particular concerns right now.

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Other, General Information about SCPs with abilities.

Elevator Pitch:

  • A Watch the can open portal in space and time allowing the user to travel through time and even

different dimensions (dimensions only if the user has seen the dimension.

  • A Old Black and White Tv that houses the sales commercial for the watch in a form of a 80's style

advertisement.

  • A Male salesman in the commercial that will hand you the watch if the viewer wishes to purchase

the watch for $15.99.

  • Tv will go dormant for a few months after a purchase is made.

Central Narrative: A Watch that can create portals through space and time sold to a viewer through a black and white tv by a 1.3m tall white male with bold hair and blue eyes. After the "salesman" finishes talking about the product he will ask the viewer if they would like to purchase the watch. If the viewer agrees then the salesman will reach id hand through the tv maintaining the black and white texture and ask for a payment of $15.99. Once payed the salesman will place the money into his pocket and hand a box to the viewer then the TV will turn off and remain dormant for 2-3 months.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As far as I know there isn't really anything like this but the concept I think is pretty interesting because of how the object is obtained and what it can do. This is why i will require clearance level 4 in order to interact with the watch, tv or salesman and the SCP will receive a safe class because it's not going anywhere without help.

Additional Notes: I'm wondering if there is anything like this already on the site, if it's a good and article worthy subject and if there is anything about the SCP that would benefit from change, keep in mind i wish to keep this a safe or thaumiel class SCP. Thankyou :)

item.title: Re: A Balkan fairy tail
item.content:encoded:
Since no one else decided to crit this I guess I will.

+ show block
– hide block

The story is set in the Bosnian war. A girl with powers of a fairy is found in Bosnia. The Balkan MTF force captures her.

I'm sorry if I have no familiarity with the Bosnian war the Balkan MTF (is that an already existing MTF or is it a new one you made for this skip?) or what Balkan is. Also, what do you mean by "powers of a fairy", can you elaborate?

Agent Kosta, an ethnic Croat born in Canada is sent to recover her but the Balkan base is attacked by the Chaos insurgency. The battle ends with Kosta and one insurgent as the only survivors. Kosta grabs the girl and they go through the war-torn Bosnia, trying to reach the Croatian coast while running from the still alive insurgent.

A Croat born in Canada? You can just say she has Croat ethnicity ya know, don't need to use more words than you need to or just generally unimportant info.

So MTF Balkan has a base? I don't really think MTF's have their own proper bases, remember these guys are a Mobile Task Force, they move around a lot when needed to, not sure why they would have a central base.

I'm getting some big Life Is Strange 2 vibes, a normal human-being running away with a person that has extra-ordinary abilities to evade capture or worse. And didn't you just say that Kosta was the only survivor but now you're saying they're running away with the kid?

As they drive through Bosnia, Kosta starts to bond with the kid. The child doesn't speak but communicates with Kosta by creating pictures on the various surfaces with her fairy dust. They meet various individuals from all three sides of the Bosnian conflict.

Yeah, I'm getting more Life Is Strange 2 vibes from this, they meet people on their journey, some helpful and some not. By the way, I see no reason for the fairy dust scene being described here, remember the central narrative goes over the main story beats and what you intend on going for, not a 1-1 synopsis of every minute plot detail.

In an abandoned coffy bar "Amsterdam", where all of the ethnicities laugh and drink together, while the girl, now going by the name Bojana Skadaric, plays with the other kids, he gets drunk and tells the sad fate of his wife, and how he lost her in a mission. His best friend Sam blamed him for her loss and they never saw each other again.

Ok, this is where I'm gonna start to nitpick further. If you're trying to go for a sense of peace and serenity with this, I get what you're trying to do, but the whole "all ethnicities" thing just feels a bit forced and shoved in there to show for it? Don't take this as me being blatantly offensive or something because I'm truly NOT trying to come off like that, I don't know it just feels a bit out of touch and cliche. It kind of just comes off as your version of "I can just show peace and harmony by plopping a bunch of diverse characters with different ethnicities, religions, and sexual orientations all in one place getting along!"

Why did the girl's name change? Why didn't she share or have a name before? Is it because she was previously an inhabitant of the forest that can not be named?

Are they a he or a she? I'm just gonna call them Bojana. So Bojana is a kid..but gets drunk and mourns their wife..in front of the other kids? Why is this whole mission subplot even here or mentioned? It doesn't add anything to the story or the anomaly.

The insurgent attacks the pub and destroys it. They reach an area controlled by a Croatian warlord "Swedish" that commands a volunteer division while the local official army unwillingly follows his orders. Swedish is in a blood feud with a local Serbian warlord. He finds out about the fairy abilities of the girl, as she intervened in an execution, but before he could capture her the Serbs start an offensive and the Serbian commander challenges Swedish to come out.

Yeah I highly doubt a sole CI could wipe out an entire hub with a fairy in it, let alone destroy the ENTIRE pub, we're talking about one guy here. On to the Swedish stuff, "commands a volunteer division while the local official army unwillingly follow his orders", so basically a militia made up of civilians and corrupt army officials? That's probably a better and simpler way to describe it.

I don't know what to say about the rest, we'll see.

Enraged, Swedish leads the volunteers to battle. The leader of the official army realises that his commander went completely insane, and orders the evacuation of the village.

I still have no idea what to say, can't bite on this.

Kosta and Bojana go to the evacuation truck and are stoped by the voice of the chaos insurgent who calls Kosta by name, it is Sam. As he leaves to confront his former friend he tells the army leader to go far away with Bojana. He and Sam have only one bullet each and as they fire at each other a bomb drops between them, ending the footage.

…This just sounds so underwhelming and cliche. Do you think the Chaos Insurgency just goes recruiting for agents on the fly? Sure I guess the mission stuff would cause a lot of animosity between Sam and Kosta but the fact that Sam somehow joined the CI because of it is literally so unrealistic, not just in-universe but irl. If you're working for the Foundation and you hear there's a splinter group that is actively engaging in attacks on the Foundation, who's firepower and military strength is larger than some countries, and they're actively terminating members of the CI as well, I wouldn't think twice of burying the possibility of me joining the CI to the ground.

WHY HAS THIS ENTIRE ORDEAL EVEN BEEN RECORDED, HOW WOULD THIS LOOK IN THE ARTICLE, WHY IS THIS BEING CONTAINED AS ANOMALY WHEN IT'S LITERALLY JUST REGULAR FOUND FOOTAGE ABOUT A FAIRY

I can't bite on any of this.


tl;dr: I feel as though this is severely lacking in plot, there's incredibly cliche tropes in here, things that make 0 sense, and a feeling of more to be desired (and not in the good way).

I'm sorry if this sounds a bit vehement, I just wanted to be as honest and helpful as possible, since English probably isn't your first language I understand if that's why there were grammatical and wording errors. Have a good one.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The sword can drain exact amounts of blood, and heal wounds perfectly once the blood is lost. The longbow can shoot arrows at unnatural speeds and the arrows can always hit their mark. The armor is from a time period that didn't exist when it was made, and can't be destroyed.

It's more that the piece wants to be about a gut reaction, but also wants to make enough of a gesture to a story that it's not entirely barren. Frankly the contents of the piece are just "here's the basic, pared-down list of things the Foundation would do differently in this situation," to shuffle the reader along to the point where their existence is terminated between pages loading. I'm sorry it didn't work for you, but it's pretty much working as intended I think. If it ends up lasting, that's cool, if it crashes and burns, that just means one of the two reactions I figured it would get turns out to represent more people than the other. Which will be educational for me at least :P
